description: conj:e-hartree-categorical-derivation round 19: closes the two outstanding computational steps of rounds 17-18, exactly.  (R1) The bare molecular-braid characters are the classical Hecke-Coxeter hook-support values chi_{(a,1^{4-a})}(c) = (-1)^{4-a} q^{2a-5} — round-17's numerical table is exact for all q and the (2,2) zero is the hook-support theorem (Ram 1991 q-Murnaghan-Nakayama); the bare product chi_{(3,1)} chi_{(2,1,1)} = -1 exactly, so the R18 hoped-for delta_q-magnitude identification is refuted at the bare level (the bare characters carry channel SUPPORT only).  (R2) Dressing sigma_2 with eigenvalues (q^m, -q^{-m}) is affine (A_m = h[m-1]_q/[2]_q, B_m = (q^m+q^{-m})/[2]_q-normalised), so by character linearity the scalar block ACTIVATES: chi_{(2,2)}(dressed) = h[m-1]_q[4]_q/[2]_q^2 (nonzero for all m >= 2), and at the K-shell power m = 5 equals h([4]_q/[2]_q)^2 = h (dim_q V_{(2,2)})^2 — the Plancherel square of the scalar block's q-dimension, a q-dim-layer quantity surfacing in the Markov layer exactly at m-1 = n = 4.  Restriction values chi(sigma_1 sigma_3) derived by Littlewood-Richardson to H_2 x H_2 (q -> 1 recovers the S_4 (12)(34) column).  The alpha_EM^2 magnitude chain is NOT produced (h^1 x dim_q^2, not h^4/delta^2 delta^2): the conjecture remains OPEN with the gap localised to the archimedean trace-ratio on the activated scalar block.
